characters.description: Ambiguously Brown:Which actually makes a certain amount of senseif he is supposed to be descended from Egyptian immigrants; the country's population has always been a mix of Arabic and African ethnicities, with a number of Caucasians after it ended up becoming part of the British Empire. Arbitrary Skepticism: In the premiere, he witnesses (among other things) mummies coming to life, a man turning into what looks like a bug monster, and statue-like warriors running around all over the place... butbelieving he is the reincarnation of a long dead Egyptian prince?Pfft.No way. Broken Pedestal: When he learns his fathertook a job for Scarab, he's understandably pretty upset. The Chosen One: He is the reincarnation of Prince Rapses, whose "spirit" Scarab wishes to consume in order to achieve immortality. Distracted by the Sexy:In both his encounters with Chontra he ends up having a crush on her.

characters.name: Presley Carnovan
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown:Which actually makes a certain amount of senseif he is supposed to be descended from Egyptian immigrants; the country's population has always been a mix of Arabic and African ethnicities, with a number of Caucasians after it ended up becoming part of the British Empire. Arbitrary Skepticism: In the premiere, he witnesses (among other things) mummies coming to life, a man turning into what looks like a bug monster, and statue-like warriors running around all over the place... butbelieving he is the reincarnation of a long dead Egyptian prince?Pfft.No way. Broken Pedestal: When he learns his fathertook a job for Scarab, he's understandably pretty upset. The Chosen One: He is the reincarnation of Prince Rapses, whose "spirit" Scarab wishes to consume in order to achieve immortality. Distracted by the Sexy:In both his encounters with Chontra he ends up having a crush on her.

characters.name: Ja-Kal
characters.description: Arrows on Fire: His bow can fire flaming arrows. Bat Deduction: His tracking skills are so good both Presley and Armon can't help but notice:Rapses is right Ja-Kal, youaregood. Being Good Sucks: He'd love more than anything to be reunited with his wife and son in the afterlife, but he puts being Presley's protector first. He also wants to embrace his revived nephew, but he can't risk revealing their base's location.Ja-Kal:Must my duties always come first? I've given up so much for my pharaoh already. First my brother. Then my family. My life. Cain and Abel: The noble Abel to Arakh's treacherous and resentful Cain. Further solidified in that Arakh slew Ja-Kal personally, which is how he became a mummy to begin with. Fatal Flaw:Pride. Ja-Kal is deeply honorable, but that honor can turn into a kind of stubborness that prevents him from asking for help himself. He really suffers for it in "Missing Ja-Kal" when Scarab performs a mystical attack on his animal totem; he's left suffering loss of muscle control and painful seizures, but he'd rather endanger himself trying to fix the problem alone than ask for help. Scarab mocks this as a warrior's pride, though Ja-Kal ultimately swallows his pride in the end.

characters.name: Armon
characters.description: Artificial Limbs: When transformed, Armon acquires a golden arm. He treasures it very highly, since it was a gift from the pharaoh himself. Bare-Fisted Monk: Unlike the other Mummies, Armon is a master of hand-to-hand combat and doesn't use any weapons. Back when he was alive, he was in charge of training Rapses in Egypt-Tsu, and he takes up the same role with Presley. Big Eater: Pretty much every episode has him either eating or expressing a desire to eat. Furthermore, he'll eat pretty much anything. The Big Guy: The biggest and the strongest of the Mummies. Boisterous Bruiser: Armon is the most jovial of the four Mummies both in battle and outside of it.

characters.name: Rath
characters.description: Animal Motifs: Rath's a cobra. Badass Bookworm: He is the smartest of the mummies, and a decent fighter. Bungling Inventor: Rath's inventions have a tendency to go haywire for one reason or another. For instance, in "Married to the Geb", he repairs a vacuum cleaner, only for it to start running amuck and trying to eat Kahti. In addition, aRunning Gaginvolves him being inspired to invent something new, not realizing that what he's made already exists in the modern day. Butt-Monkey: He's easily the most accident-prone of the four mummies, from getting hit by potshots from Scarab's mooks to losing his memory and in one episode, getting abducted by government agents who mistaken him to bean alien. The opening credits seems to drill this in by playing a clip from one of the episodes: Ja-kal and Rath gets shot out of the sky, Armon managed to grab Ja-kal... while Rath hits the floor just two feet away. Death by Origin Story: He and all the other mummies on his team died before the series even started.

characters.name: Nefertina
characters.description: Absurdly Sharp Claws: Aside from her whip, Nefertina's gauntlets have claws strong enough to shatter a Shabti. Action Girl: Nefertina, who fights right alongside the other three guardians of prince Rapses and even disguised herself as a guy to ride chariots in ancient Egypt. Is inexplicably still mistaken for a guy on occasion. Animal Motifs: Her armor has a cat motif. Badass Driver: She enjoyed chariot racing in ancient Egypt, and this carries over to her being the main pilot of the team's vehicles in the modern day. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Her bandages stop below her chest to show off some (blue) skin, whereas the three male mummies are bandaged all the way down to the waist.

characters.name: Kahti
characters.description: Badass Adorable: She's a cat that can transform. Death by Origin Story: She, like Presley's mummy protectors, died and was mummified before the series even started. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Most of the time anyway. Loyal Animal Companion: For the mummies and Presley. Team Pet: For the mummies and Presley.

characters.name: Scarab
characters.description: Big Bad: He's the main antagonist of the series. Bullying a Dragon: A frequent cause of his plans going awry; in his arrogance, he unintentionally insults the various spirits and gods he summons, all of whom are more powerful than him. The Chessmaster: Frequently. Scarab has dozens of plans that are frequently years, if not centuries in the works. Creepy Monotone: Scarab rarely rases his voice above a eerie monotone. Dead Person Impersonation: The original Harris Stone was an archeologist who discovered Scarab's tomb in 1928. Scarab murdered Stone and posed as him since then, continuing the archaeologist's career for his own ends and becoming a wealthy man in the process.

characters.name: Heka
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: Heka is never without a witty remark, often at Scarab's expense. Only Sane Woman: Her insults at Scarab's expense frequently highlight the absurdity of a given scheme or the inevitable failure. Playing with Fire: She can spit fire. Serpent Staff: In battle, Heka becomes a snake-like staff which shootsfireor purple energy blasts. Servile Snarker: For Scarab.

characters.name: Ammut
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: Ammut was a neutral figure in Egyptian mythology. Gender Flip: Ammut is a male here. Ammut was female in Egyptian mythology. Mix-and-Match Critter: Akin to his mythological basis, Ammut is a chimera with a crocodile's head, a lion's mane and forepaws and a hippo's hindquarters.

characters.name: Set
characters.description: Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: He and Anubis can be amazingly competent, under the right circumstances. I Have Many Names: Dog of the Desert, Master of Evil and Lord of Thunder. He lists these off to Scarab in "Brother's Keeper" when the latter enrages him. Never My Fault: He always blames Anubis whenever anything goes wrong. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: He obeys Scarab's orders because he was summoned to do so, but he's quick to bark back (pun intended) if Scarab insults him.

characters.name: Anubis
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: Anubis was a benevolent god in Egyptian mythology, and Set disowned him for choosing to side with Horus. Beware the Silly Ones: He spends more time acting silly than actually fighting, but when he does fight he's quite clearly out of the Mummies' league. Everyone Hates Hades: From a neutral, if benevolent character in the original myths to a lesser villain in the series. Not-So-Harmless Villain: Unfortunately for him and his partner Set, he's not very consistent.

characters.name: Talos
characters.description: Artificial Human: Made out of bronze. Blood Knight: Loves fighting to the point that he once refused to stand down after Scarab ordered him to. Evil Counterpart: To Armonuntil his last appearance. Giant Mook: Scarab recreates Talos in modern times and enlists his help in fighting Armon in a gladitorial ring. Heel–Face Turn: After hefell forthe city of San Francisco's "Statue of Freedom".

characters.name: Chontra
characters.description: Cute Witch: In her child form, which she once again used to get close to Presley. Dating Catwoman: With Rath before the start of the series. Distaff Counterpart: To Rath, both of them being (relatively) attractive sorcerers who fight with magic in battle. Hot Teacher: Disguises herself as this to get close to Presley and use him to get at Rath. Presley's mother even suspects her son is having a crush on her. Hot Witch: She is a very attractive sorceress.

characters.name: Arakh
characters.description: Always Someone Better: The source of his hatred for Ja-Kal is that the latter always outshone him; first at home for their father's attention then when Ja-Kal was made captain of the hunt, a position Arakh coveted. Cain and Abel: The resentful, spiteful Cain to his heroic brother Ja-Kal's Abel. Furthering the comparison, it was Arakh himself who slew Ja-Kal back in Egyptian times. Eyepatch of Power: Arakh lost his left eye while fighting a lion and has to wear an eyepatch to cover up the injury. Manipulative Bastard: Emotionally manipulates his son Kimas into assisting him against his own uncle. Red and Black and Evil All Over: His armor is red and black.

characters.name: The Mummies in General
characters.description: Arbitrary Skepticism: Even when they're able to accept the idea of cars and technology in general, Presley's attempts to explain modern science to them just make them laugh as if it were the funniest thing in the world.Justifiedin that they're thirty-five thousand years out of time and view everything through the lens of mysticism. Artistic License – Biology: While acknowledging on occasion that the mummies are technically dead, their need for food appears genuine rather than purely psychological. When Rath and Armon swapped bodies in "Who's Who?", for instance, Armon-in-Rath felt less inclined to gormandize, while while Rath-in Armon feels Armon's hunger pains, neither of which would apply if they just ate because they wanted to rather than because they had to. Battle Cry: "Let's kick Tut!", usually shouted after transforming. Color-Coded Characters: Each Mummy is associated with a specific colour: Blue for Ja-Kal, Purple for Armon, Green for Rath and Red for Nefertina. Henshin Hero: By shouting out "With the strength of Ra!", the Mummies change into their armoured forms.

characters.name: Kimas
characters.description: Big Eater: Devours his first burger in one gulp, wrapper and all, much to Armon's approval. Heel–Face Revolving Door: He initially blows off Scarab due to not liking him, but then rejoins when he feels Ja-Kal isn't respecting him. When he finally learns how consumed by vengeance his father is, he pulles a genuineHeel–Face Turn. Impossibly Tacky Clothes: When going about in the city, he wears a long trenchcoat, a wide-brimmed sun hat andenormoussunglasses. It just makes him stick out all the more. Scary Scorpions: Like his father, he dons scorpion-themed armor.Downplayedin that he's not truly evil, just moody. Teens Are Angsty: Essentially a moody teen in a thirty-five thousand year old body.
